41824-hogarth.title: Hogarth
41824-hogarth.creator: Unknown
41824-hogarth.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The auction was proceeding leisurely and without excitement. It was an “off day.” I was present because these pictures of the Early British School included a “Conversation Piece” ascribed to Hogarth, and a medley of prints after him, worn impressions, the vigour gone, merely the skeletons of his bustling designs remaining. They fetched trivial prices: they were not the real thing.

4744-ten-nights-in-a-bar-room.title: Ten Nights In A Bar Room
4744-ten-nights-in-a-bar-room.creator: Unknown
4744-ten-nights-in-a-bar-room.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "Temptation!" The open brows of Simon Slade contracted a little. "No, sir!" he replied, emphatically. "The till is safer under his care than it would be in that of one man in ten. The boy comes, sir, of honest parents. Simon Slade never wronged anybody out of a farthing."

arxiv-1802-00756.title: Infinitary and Cyclic Proof Systems for Transitive Closure Logic
arxiv-1802-00756.creator: Liron Cohen, Reuben N. S. Rowe
arxiv-1802-00756.description: Abstract Transitive closure logic is a known extension of first-order logic obtained by introducing a transitive closure operator. While other extensions of first-order logic with inductive definitions are a priori parametrized by a set of inductive definitions, the addition of the transitive closure operator uniformly captures all finitary inductive definitions.

arxiv-1909-13149.title: Morse-Smale surfaced diffeomorphisms with orientable heteroclinic
arxiv-1909-13149.creator: A. Morozov, O. Pochinka
arxiv-1909-13149.description: Abstract In the present paper we consider preserving orientation Morse-Smale diffeomorphisms on surfaces. Using the methods of factorization and linearizing neighborhoods we prove that such diffeomorphisms have a finite number of orientable heteroclinic orbits. \currentvolume 18 \currentnumber 1 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 53C17, 22E30, 49J15 1. Introduction The Morse-Smale dynamics is a pattern of a regular structurally stable (rough) behaviour.

arxiv-2108-09458.title: Scattering and Strebel graphs
arxiv-2108-09458.description: Abstract We consider a special scattering experiment with n particles in ℝ 1 , n − 3 \mathbb{R}^{1,n-3} . The scattering equations in this set-up become the saddle-point equations of a Penner-like matrix model, where in the large n n limit, the spectral curve is directly related to the unique Strebel differential on a Riemann sphere with three punctures.

arxiv-2310-09914.title: Kinetic glass transition in granular gases and nonlinear molecular fluids
arxiv-2310-09914.creator: A. Patrón, B. Sánchez-Rey, A. Prados
arxiv-2310-09914.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. Patrón, B. Sánchez-Rey, A. Prados. In this paper we investigate, both analytically and numerically, the emergence of a kinetic glass transition in two different model systems: a uniformly heated granular gas and a molecular fluid with nonlinear drag. Despite the profound differences between these two physical systems, their behavior in thermal cycles share strong similarities, which stem from the relaxation time diverging algebraically at low temperatures for both systems.

arxiv-2411-02504.title: Scattering of Quantum Particles in Global de Sitter Spacetime I: The Formalism
arxiv-2411-02504.creator: Tomasz R. Taylor 1,2 , Bin Zhu 3 1 Department of Physics, Northeastern University, Boston, MA 02115, USA 2 Faculty of Physics, University of Warsaw, Pasteura 5, 02-093 Warsaw, Poland 3 School of Mathematics and Maxwell Institute for Mathematical Sciences, University of Edinburgh, EH9 3FD, UK
arxiv-2411-02504.description: Abstract We develop a formalism for computing the scattering amplitudes in maximally symmetric de Sitter spacetime with compact spatial dimensions. We describe quantum states by using the representation theory of de Sitter symmetry group and link the Hilbert space to “inertial” geodesic observers.

arxiv-2502-19642.title: cMIM: A Contrastive Mutual Information Framework for Unified Generative and Discriminative Representation Learning
arxiv-2502-19642.creator: Micha Livne
arxiv-2502-19642.description: Abstract Learning representations that are useful for unknown downstream tasks is a fundamental challenge in representation learning. Prominent approaches in this domain include contrastive learning, self-supervised masking, and denoising auto-encoders. In this paper, we introduce a novel method, termed contrastive Mutual Information Machine (cMIM), which aims to enhance the utility of learned representations for downstream tasks.

arxiv-2504-17772.title: Demagnetization in micromagnetics: magnetostatic self-interactions of bulk chiral magnetic skyrmions
arxiv-2504-17772.creator: Paul Leask, Martin Speight
arxiv-2504-17772.description: Abstract We develop a theoretical and numerical framework for three-dimensional bulk chiral magnets that includes the full magnetostatic dipole-dipole interaction and its back-reaction on the magnetization. Assuming translational invariance along one spatial direction, we analyze the effect of dipolar interactions on three Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) terms – Dresselhaus, Rashba, and Heusler –corresponding to Bloch, Néel, and antiskyrmion textures.

arxiv-2507-10172.title: Play Style Identification Using Low-Level Representations of Play Traces in MicroRTS Thanks: Short Paper. This work was supported by the EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Intelligent Games & Game Intelligence (IGGI) EP/S022325/1
arxiv-2507-10172.creator: Ruizhe Yu Xia, Jeremy Gow, Simon Lucas
arxiv-2507-10172.description: Abstract Play style identification can provide valuable game design insights and enable adaptive experiences, with the potential to improve game playing agents. Previous work relies on domain knowledge to construct play trace representations using handcrafted features. More recent approaches incorporate the sequential structure of play traces but still require some level of domain abstraction.

arxiv-2507-21107.title: Curved Inference
arxiv-2507-21107.creator: Rob Manson (https://robman.fyi)
arxiv-2507-21107.description: Abstract Abstract We propose Curved Inference - a geometric Interpretability framework that tracks how the residual stream trajectory of a large language model bends in response to shifts in semantic concern. Across 20 matched prompts spanning emotional, moral, perspective, logical, identity, environmental, and nonsense domains, we analyse Gemma3-1b and LLaMA3.

arxiv-2601-00868.title: SmartFlow: Reinforcement Learning and Agentic AI for Bike-Sharing Optimisation Publication type: Research Article/Editorial
arxiv-2601-00868.creator: Aditya Sreevatsa K, Arun Kumar Raveendran, Jesrael K Mani, Prakash G Shigli, Rajkumar Rangadore, Narayana Darapaneni, Anwesh Reddy Paduri \fnoteref 1
arxiv-2601-00868.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Aditya Sreevatsa K, Arun Kumar Raveendran, Jesrael K Mani, Prakash G Shigli, Rajkumar Rangadore, Narayana Darapaneni, Anwesh Reddy Paduri \fnoteref 1. SmartFlow is a multi-layered framework that integrates Reinforcement Learning and Agentic AI to address the dynamic rebalancing problem in urban bike-sharing services. Its architecture separates strategic, tactical, and communication functions for clarity and scalability.

pmc-10554722.title: FRI407 Identification Of AIPB Expression For Early Breast Cancer Prediction
pmc-10554722.creator: Nicole Elizabeth Doetch, Himangshu S Bose
pmc-10554722.description: Disclosure: N.E. Doetch: None. H.S. Bose: None.The incidence of developing invasive breast cancer in women is about 14% during their lifetime and accounts for over 16% of all female cancers. Breast cancer is categorized based on the presence and absence of receptors including Estrogen Receptor (ER+/-), Progesterone Receptor (PR+/-), and Human Epidermal Growth Factor 2 Receptor (HER2+/-).

pmc-10685686.title: Sclerodermatous Graft-Versus-Host Disease: A Rare Sequela of Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation
pmc-10685686.creator: Mohamad Jabin, Sonali Batta, Madeeha Mian, Palak Parekh
pmc-10685686.description: Although graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a common immunologic reaction after an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT), progression into sclerodermatous GVHD is a rare sequela. It can present locally or generalized with various cutaneous and mucocutaneous manifestations, resulting in loss of skin elasticity and reduced functional capabilities.

pmc-11437828.title: Differential susceptibility of human motor neurons to infection with Usutu and West Nile virus
pmc-11437828.creator: Eleanor M Marshall, Lisa Bauer, Tessa Nelemans, Syriam Sooksawasdi Na Ayudhya, Feline Benavides, Kristina Lanko, Femke M S de Vrij, Steven A Kushner, Marion Koopmans, Debby van Riel, Barry Rockx
pmc-11437828.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) are closely related flaviviruses with differing capacities to cause neurological disease in humans. WNV is thought to use a transneural route of neuroinvasion along motor neurons and causes severe motor deficits. The potential for use of transneural routes of neuroinvasion by USUV has not been investigated experimentally, and evidence from the few clinical case reports of USUV-associated neuroinvasive disease is lacking.

pmc-11635837.title: Mucosal vaccination with outer membrane vesicles derived from Bordetella pertussis reduces nasal bacterial colonization after experimental infection
pmc-11635837.creator: E. Rudi, E. Gaillard, D. Bottero, T. Ebensen, C. A. Guzman, Daniela Hozbor
pmc-11635837.description: IntroductionWe previously identified Bordetella pertussis-derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) as a promising immunogen for improving pertussis vaccines. In this study, we evaluated the efficacy of our vaccine prototype in immunization strategies aimed at reducing disease transmission by targeting colonization in the upper airways while maintaining protection against severe disease by reducing colonization in the lower respiratory tract.

pmc-11683667.title: Tumor Expression of CD83 Reduces Glioma Progression and Is Associated with Reduced Immunosuppression
pmc-11683667.creator: Malcolm F. McDonald, Rachel Naomi Curry, Isabella O’Reilly, Brittney Lozzi, Alexis Cervantes, Zhung-Fu Lee, Anna Rosenbaum, Peihao He, Carrie Mohila, Arif O. Harmanci, Akdes Serin Harmanci, Benjamin Deneen, Ganesh Rao
pmc-11683667.description: Malignant glioma, the most lethal form of brain cancer, presents with an immunosuppressive microenvironment that obstructs tumor cell clearance and hampers immunotherapeutic interventions. Despite advancements in characterizing cellular and extracellular profiles in cancer, the immunosuppressive mechanisms specific to glioma remain poorly understood.

pmc-12382282.title: GeneBits: ultra-sensitive tumour-informed ctDNA monitoring of treatment response and relapse in cancer patients
pmc-12382282.creator: Julian Broche, Olga Kelemen, Aishwarya Sekar, Leon Schütz, Francesc Muyas, Andrea Forschner, Christopher Schroeder, Stephan Ossowski
pmc-12382282.description: BackgroundCirculating tumour DNA (ctDNA) in liquid biopsies has emerged as a powerful biomarker in cancer patients. Its relative abundance in cell-free DNA serves as a proxy for the overall tumour burden. Here we present GeneBits, a method for cancer therapy monitoring and relapse detection.

pmc-12615818.title: Epidemiology of work-related incidents in healthcare: findings from a 7-year retrospective review of work-related incidents in a tertiary hospital in Singapore
pmc-12615818.creator: Kenneth Bao Ren Leong, Wai Kuen Kam, Shu Rong Lim, Prahlad Govinda Krishnan, Xiaohui Xin, Soo Bee Tan, Alicia S T Loi, John Wah Lim, Wee Hoe Gan
pmc-12615818.description: Healthcare workers are exposed to various occupational risks. Due to the high workloads, staff shortages and the COVID-19 pandemic, healthcare workers (HCWs) are at an elevated risk of work-related incidents. This study aims to describe the epidemiology of work-related incidents in a tertiary hospital providing acute care in Singapore; and to analyse those incidents that are of increasing concern.

pmc-13196370.title: S-acylation and membrane localization of the small GTPase ARL15 are mediated by the Golgi S-acyltransferases ZDHHC7 and ZDHHC3
pmc-13196370.creator: Takeshi Chino, Makoto Araki, Yuki Ashi, Yusuke Izawa, Yuji Nunami, Yosuke Ichikawa, Itsuki Kuroiwa, Kenji Kontani
pmc-13196370.description: ARL15 is a member of the ARF-like (ARL) family of small GTPases, implicated in the regulation of ion homeostasis and metabolic signaling pathways. Although ARL15 has been suggested to undergo S-acylation—a reversible lipid modification that governs membrane association and trafficking—the stoichiometry of this modification and the responsible S-acyltransferases have remained unclear.

pmc-13459563.title: PROSPER: a phase III trial of lecithinized superoxide dismutase to prevent oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with colorectal cancer
pmc-13459563.creator: K. Yamazaki, T. Kato, T. Yamada, K. Ogihara, T. Ishikawa, N. Ishizuka, T. Yoshino, K. Yamaguchi, T. Mizushima
pmc-13459563.description: BackgroundOxaliplatin-based chemotherapy is a standard adjuvant therapy for stage II or stage III colorectal cancer (CRC); however, its use is limited by chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), which reduces the quality of life of patients and often persists for months or years after chemotherapy ends.

pmc-13465304.title: Prophylactic bi-level non-invasive positive pressure ventilation during monitored anesthesia care for transfemoral TAVI in a morbidly obese patient with obstructive sleep apnea: a case report
pmc-13465304.creator: Saad Ahmed Naved, Madiha Khan, Saad Rasool, Muhammad Zameer Rajput
pmc-13465304.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTranscatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed under monitored anesthesia care (MAC); however, its use in patients with morbid obesity and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains challenging because of the risk of hypoventilation and airway compromise.
